sourcedFrom: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) (2025)
cleanIntro: ⛔ This is a four-screw-and-done gun by design. Pardini's whole published strip is: magazine out, one hex screw under the muzzle, barrel-and-bolt off the frame, bolt off the barrel. The Rapid Fire runs .22 Short and sees the highest round counts of any pistol in this catalog, so the 500-round bore interval and the 5,000-round magazine strip are not conservative advice — they arrive fast. Keep the muzzle DOWN for the entire job — the book says so for both directions — and keep every solvent and every drop of oil away from the trigger unit, which is a gram-scale adjustable mechanism and the reason you own the pistol.

steps.title: Magazine out FIRST, and prove the chamber — the book says so twice
steps.action: Drop the magazine before anything else, then look and feel into the open breech. Pardini repeats this instruction as a WARNING one line below the strip procedure, which is the manual telling you where people go wrong: the takedown screw is easy to reach with a magazine still in the well.
steps.caution: It is extremely important to remember to remove the magazine before attempting to dismantle the pistol.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and ‘prove’ the pistol safe.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING, REASSEMBLY, CLEANING AND LUBRIFICATION, printed p.30

steps.title: Muzzle DOWN for the whole job
steps.action: Turn the pistol so the muzzle points at the floor and keep it there through the strip and the rebuild. This is not just muzzle discipline — the barrel-and-bolt group comes off the frame as a loose assembly and the recoil spring rides with it, so pointing down is what stops the parts leaving the gun in the wrong order.
steps.quote: Both, dismantiling and reassembly should be carried out with the pistol pointing downwards.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING, REASSEMBLY, CLEANING AND LUBRIFICATION — WARNING, printed p.30

steps.title: One hex screw under the muzzle — that is the whole takedown
steps.action: There is a single hexagonal screw under the muzzle. Undo it and take it right out; there is no lever, no catch and no second fastener. Put the screw somewhere it cannot roll — it is small, and it is the only thing holding the top group on.
steps.quote: Undo and remove the hexagonal screw under the muzzle 2.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING, REASSEMBLY, CLEANING AND LUBRIFICATION, printed p.30

steps.title: Barrel and bolt come off together, forward and up
steps.action: Still pointing down, draw the combined barrel-and-bolt assembly off the frame. It should come away without force. If it fights you, the hex screw is not fully out — do not lever it, back the screw out further.
steps.quote: With the pistol pointing downwards carefully, pull off the combined
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING, REASSEMBLY, CLEANING AND LUBRIFICATION, printed p.30

steps.title: Bolt off the barrel unit — and that is as far as the book goes
steps.action: Separate the bolt from the barrel unit. That is the end of the published strip: four operations, no trigger group, no frame internals. Everything past this point is a gunsmith job in Pardini's own terms, and the warranty says work must be done at Pardini or by someone they authorise.
steps.quote: Separate the bolt from the barrel unit.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING, REASSEMBLY, CLEANING AND LUBRIFICATION, printed p.30

steps.title: Brass brush the chamber and bore, then patch — and hunt the lead
steps.action: Run a correctly sized brass brush through the chamber and bore, then follow with a patch. Pardini names lead specifically: a .22 match barrel leads at the throat first and a leaded throat costs accuracy before it costs function, which is the whole point of a gun like this. Do it at 500 rounds, not when it feels dirty.
steps.aside: Check that all lead is removed to insure top accuracy and function.
steps.quote: It is recommended to do it no later than 500 shots use first a properly sized brass brush on the chamber and bore and then clean the bore with a patch.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, printed p.30

steps.title: Lubricate only where the bolt rides — and keep it off the trigger
steps.action: A plain lubricant, no additives, on the contact points: where the bolt runs on the barrel and on the guide pins. Nothing goes near the trigger mechanism. Pardini's trigger is a multi-screw adjustable unit set to grams; oil in it collects grit and changes the let-off you spent a season finding.
steps.quote: Lubrificate the contact points (where the bolt rides on the barrel and guide pins) with a simple lubricant with no additive. Do not use solvent or oils on the trigger mechanism.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, printed p.30

steps.title: Magazines come apart every 5,000 rounds
steps.action: The magazine is not a wipe-down item on this pistol. Pardini calls for stripping and thoroughly cleaning the magazines at 5,000 rounds — and on the SP family the EJECTOR is built into the magazine, so a fouled magazine is an ejection failure waiting to happen, not just a feeding one.
steps.quote: At least every 5.000 rounds disassemble and thoroughly clean the
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, printed p.30

steps.title: Thirteen damper rings, and they are a wear item at 15,000 shots
steps.action: The dynamic counterweight in the barrel tunnel runs on thirteen rubber damper rings, and Pardini treats them as consumables rather than fittings: replace them at about 15,000 shots. They go dead gradually, so nothing announces it — the gun simply stops settling the way it used to and shooters chase it in the trigger instead.
steps.quote: It is recommended to replace the 13 damper ringhs
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — Counterweight / RINGS, printed p.28

steps.title: Reverse order, and watch the recoil spring seat
steps.action: Rebuild in the reverse order, muzzle still down. The one thing the book singles out is the recoil spring: it has to be correctly fitted before the top group goes home. A spring that is off its seat will let the assembly sit down and even let the screw start, and you will not find out until the first shot short-strokes.
steps.quote: Pay particular attention that the recoil spring is correctly fitted when reassembling.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi Instruction Manual — SP, SP HI-TECH, SP Rapid Fire, SP Rapid Fire HI-TECH, HP — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING, REASSEMBLY, CLEANING AND LUBRIFICATION — WARNING, printed p.30

deepAbsentReason: Pardini publishes NO deeper strip for this pistol. The book's dismantling section is four operations long — magazine out, hex screw out, barrel-and-bolt off, bolt off the barrel — and then stops. There is no published route into the trigger unit, the frame or the sear, and the trigger section that follows is an ADJUSTMENT chapter (seven named screws, quarter-turn at a time), not a disassembly one. ⛔ That is a real limit and not an oversight: Pardini's warranty states that all warranty interventions must be done at Pardini Armi or by a firm they authorise, and the same page disclaims liability for repairs done by unauthorised persons. So the deep clean here is the magazine strip at 5,000 rounds, which the book DOES publish, and it is carried in the routine list above rather than hidden behind a paywall of invention.

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & BORE
tasks: Properly sized brass brush, chamber first then bore
⛔ All lead removed — Pardini ties this to accuracy AND function

cleaning.name: BOLT / BARREL CONTACT POINTS
tasks: Where the bolt rides on the barrel — light, additive-free lubricant
⛔ No solvent and no oil on the trigger mechanism

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES & DAMPER RINGS
tasks: Magazines stripped and thoroughly cleaned every 5,000 rounds
⚠ The ejector lives in the magazine on this family — fouling here is an ejection fault
13 counterweight damper rings replaced at about 15,000 shots

reassembly: Muzzle still pointing down for the whole rebuild.
Bolt back onto the barrel unit.
Recoil spring checked CORRECTLY SEATED before the group goes on — the one thing the book calls out.
Barrel-and-bolt assembly onto the frame, seated without force.
Hexagonal screw under the muzzle refitted and snug.
Magazine only after the pistol is together and checked.
fncheck: Back together and empty: work the bolt by hand and feel it run the full stroke without catching, then check the hex screw under the muzzle is home. Look through the bore from the breech for a patch or a brush bristle left behind. ⛔ If the bolt feels gritty or the assembly will not seat, take it apart again and look at the recoil spring — do not force the screw. Anything beyond the four published operations goes to Pardini or a firm they authorise.
